rationale: New obligation and its first check, found while pursuing the client-completion candidate: the NOOP commit that recovery broadcasts for another replica's instance can reach that instance's owner, and handleCommit's re-proposal branch dereferences leader bookkeeping that message-created records do not have. The harness drives the real handlers (handlePreAccept to create the record, then handleCommit) and observes the nil dereference instead of letting the test process die, with the client-side and history sides left out of scope. The trusted runner and a fresh correspondence review decide the formal outcome.

candidate.rationale: The obligation and binding are supplied with the check so the claim exists before the plan references it; the duty is that a legal NOOP commit must not terminate a replica that owns the instance.

question.question: A replica owns instance (0,0) but holds a record for it that a message created (no leader bookkeeping), because the instance was proposed before a restart and a recovery-led PreAccept reached it again. When a recoverer commits that instance as a single NONE command and the Commit arrives, does the handler process the commit, or does it dereference bookkeeping the record does not have and terminate the replica?
question.importance: A legal peer message that terminates a replica removes a participant from a crash-tolerant group and can repeat after every restart, turning a single recovered instance into an availability failure; the client whose operation prompted the NOOP recovery also never learns the outcome. This is a liveness/robustness duty rather than a disagreement between replicas.
contexts: instance owned by the receiving replica
record created by a message, so inst.lb is nil
commit carrying a single NONE command at or above the record's ballot
event_paths: a recovery-led PreAccept reaches the owner and creates the record through handlePreAccept
the recovery commits the instance as NOOP and broadcasts the Commit
the owner's handleCommit takes the re-proposal branch

supporting_behavior_ids.B6-commit-install: the handler under test, including the NOOP re-proposal branch
supporting_behavior_ids.B3-preaccept-recipient: creates the record without leader bookkeeping

counterevidence: scoped to the source: records created by handlePreAccept, handleAccept, handlePrepare and handleCommit leave inst.lb nil, while the re-proposal branch dereferences inst.lb.clientProposals without a nil check (S13-handleCommit, S9-handlePreAccept)
scoped to the harness: the local construction run observed a nil pointer dereference and no commit effect for a well-formed NOOP commit (record_from_message bookkeeping_nil true, then panicked true)
unknowns: whether the run loop's dispatcher contains any recover that would keep the process alive (none was found in the loop)
whether a real deployment reaches a restarted owner with an outstanding instance in its own row
question.trigger_rationale: The recovered value re-enters the normal accept and commit path (B11's attributed A1 effect), and the confirmed recovery checks show that path can commit NOOP for another replica's instance; this question asks what happens at that instance's owner when the commit is delivered, which is a distinct duty from the agreement question already decided.

obligation.description: When a replica receives a legal Commit carrying a single NONE command for an instance it owns, and its record for that instance was created by a message so that it has no leader bookkeeping, handleCommit must process the commit (install it as committed) without dereferencing the absent bookkeeping and without terminating the replica.

scope.description: One replica owning instance (0,0) whose record was created by a recovery-led PreAccept, receiving one Commit with a single NONE command at a ballot at or above its own.
assumptions: the record exists only because a message created it (newInstanceDefault leaves leader bookkeeping nil)
the commit is well formed for that instance
excluded: the client-side reaction to the missing reply
the history that made the recovering replica re-propose NOOP

grounding.derivation: handleCommit treats a NOOP commit for the replica's own row as the signal to re-propose that instance's pending client proposals, and the branch dereferences inst.lb.clientProposals. Records created by handlePreAccept, handleAccept, handlePrepare or handleCommit itself leave lb nil, so the dereference can occur on a record the protocol created from a peer message, which terminates the replica process in the run loop.
grounding.applicability: Any replication group in which a replica owns an instance it did not propose in this process lifetime (for example after a restart) and a recoverer commits NOOP for it.
unresolved: whether the run loop's lack of a recover means the panic terminates the replica process, which the harness observes only as the handler panicking
alternatives: an alternative reading is that such a record can never be the owner's, which the message-created record in this check contradicts

bindings.description: Commit installation, including the branch that re-proposes pending client proposals for a NOOP commit on the replica's own row.

associations.rationale: The branch tests commit.Replica == r.Id and a single NONE command and then dereferences inst.lb.clientProposals without checking inst.lb.
